reason: Context loss across my three daily agents is a real pain, but I already pay for GitHub Copilot Enterprise, and this is an unproven single-founder daemon I'd install from a personal brew tap or build from source, then hand every agent credential I own. The first five humans free kills the price objection, but not the trust one — I read GitHub Issues and Reddit before installing anything, and there's nothing to read yet.
objection: Giving one local daemon from an unknown founder access to all my agent credentials and code context, with no social proof on GitHub or Reddit yet.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing real teams discuss it on GitHub Issues or Reddit, plus an install path that doesn't require building from source or adding a personal brew tap.
